jori-olkkonen.name: Jori Olkkonen
jori-olkkonen.bio: Jori Olkkonen, who later used the name Petrik Salovaara, is a Finnish C64 musician, coder and scene participant known by the handle Yip. He was active through the 1980s and early 1990s, and the CCG archive links him to BMX Kidz and Uuno Turhapuro Muuttaa Maalle.

keith-miller.name: Keith Miller
keith-miller.bio: Keith Miller is a British C64-era music contributor whose documented credits include Cauldron and The Evil Dead. Surviving public biographical information is sparse, so the profile is deliberately centred on verified soundtrack credits.

keith-tinman.name: Keith Tinman
keith-tinman.bio: Keith Tinman is a British game composer associated with Odin Computer Graphics and later Ocean-era releases. His Commodore credits include Heartland, Cabal, Midnight Resistance and Toki, with work extending from original music to arrangements for home-computer conversions.

ken-lagace.name: Ken Lagace
ken-lagace.bio: Ken Lagace is an American musician, composer and programmer who worked at MicroProse during the late 1980s and early 1990s. His background also includes formal performance, teaching and orchestral work; the CCG archive links him to Airborne Ranger and Project Stealth Fighter.

kevin-a-moughtin.name: Kevin A. Moughtin
kevin-a-moughtin.bio: Kevin A. Moughtin is a British programmer, designer and musician from the early Firebird era. He created and scored Booty on the Commodore 64 and is also credited on Thunderbirds and other C64 projects, combining code, design and music rather than working only as a composer.

kris-hatlelid.name: Kris Hatlelid
kris-hatlelid.bio: Kris Hatlelid is a programmer and musician associated with Canadian C64 development, with music credits including Grand Prix Circuit, Test Drive II and other Distinctive Software-era releases. Preservation projects such as HVSC have also documented and verified his SID work, although reliable public birth details are not readily available.

mark-cooksey.name: Mark Cooksey
mark-cooksey.bio: Mark Cooksey is an English game composer and audio programmer whose best-known early work includes music for C64 arcade conversions such as Ghosts 'n Goblins, 1942, Bomb Jack and Paperboy. His career continued beyond the 8-bit era through companies including Elite and later development studios.

mark-tait.name: Mark Tait
mark-tait.bio: Mark Tait is a British game composer and sound programmer who worked with Tiertex during the late 1980s and early 1990s. His C64 credits in the CCG archive include Strider, Thunder Blade and Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade, and interviews describe his development of music tools as part of that work.

martin-galway.name: Martin Galway
martin-galway.bio: Martin Galway is a British game composer whose Commodore 64 work became strongly associated with Ocean Software. His scores and loader music include Rambo: First Blood Part II, Wizball, Green Beret and many other releases, and he became noted for technical experimentation with the SID chip, including sampled sound.

martin-iveson.name: Martin Iveson
martin-iveson.bio: Martin Iveson is an English composer and producer who entered the games industry with Core Design in the early 1990s. Alongside game music for titles including Heimdall and Agony, he later became widely known for electronic music under the name Atjazz and for running Mantis Recordings.

martin-walker.name: Martin Walker
martin-walker.bio: Martin Walker is an English programmer, composer and sound designer whose work includes a substantial body of C64 audio and technical development. He created music tools and sound routines as well as game soundtracks, with later work extending into professional audio writing and music technology.

martin-wall.name: Martin Wall
martin-wall.bio: Martin Wall is a British composer and producer who began making Amiga demo and game music in 1988 under the handle Mantronix. He later moved into commercial music production and electronic releases, while his CCG Amiga credits include Agony and RoboCop 3.
